cards.back: A tiny thing that can make you ill. Bacteria and viruses are germs.
cards.say: germ. A tiny thing that can make you ill. Bacteria and viruses are germs. Germs spread when we sneeze.

cards.back: Tiny living things. Some can make us ill, and many are helpful.
cards.say: bacteria. Tiny living things. Some can make us ill, and many are helpful. Some bacteria help to make yoghurt.

cards.back: A germ even smaller than bacteria. Viruses can cause colds and flu.
cards.say: virus. A germ even smaller than bacteria. Viruses can cause colds and flu. A cold is caused by a virus.

cards.back: An illness that stops the body from working normally.
cards.say: disease. An illness that stops the body from working normally. Measles is a disease.

cards.back: Through the air when we cough, by touch or in dirty food and water.
cards.say: How do germs spread? Through the air when we cough, by touch or in dirty food and water.

cards.front: Can germs be seen with your eyes?
cards.back: No. We need a microscope.
cards.say: Can germs be seen with your eyes? No. We need a microscope.

cards.front: How can we stop germs spreading?
cards.back: Wash hands, cover coughs, and keep food clean.
cards.say: How can we stop germs spreading? Wash hands, cover coughs, and keep food clean.

cards.back: A substance that helps the body get better or stops pain.
cards.say: medicine. A substance that helps the body get better or stops pain. Take medicine only from a trusted adult.

cards.front: Why should we only take medicine from an adult?
cards.back: Too much medicine can be harmful, so a trusted adult must give the right amount.
cards.say: Why should we only take medicine from an adult? Too much medicine can be harmful, so a trusted adult must give the right amount.

cards.back: In a safe place away from young children.
cards.say: Where should medicines be stored? In a safe place away from young children.

cards.back: A medicine that helps the body fight a germ before we get ill.
cards.say: vaccine. A medicine that helps the body fight a germ before we get ill. A vaccine protects you from measles.

cards.back: It teaches the body how to fight a germ so you are protected.
cards.say: How does a vaccine help? It teaches the body how to fight a germ so you are protected.

cards.back: A medicine that kills bacteria. It does not work on viruses.
cards.say: What is an antibiotic? A medicine that kills bacteria. It does not work on viruses.

cards.front: Why should you take all of the medicine a doctor gives you?
cards.back: To make sure all the harmful bacteria are killed, as the doctor told you.
cards.say: Why should you take all of the medicine a doctor gives you? To make sure all the harmful bacteria are killed, as the doctor told you.

cards.front: Why do we stay at home when we have a cold?
cards.back: So we do not spread the germs.
cards.say: Why do we stay at home when we have a cold? So we do not spread the germs.

cards.front: Why should we wash fruit before eating?
cards.back: To remove dirt and germs.
cards.say: Why should we wash fruit before eating? To remove dirt and germs.

cards.front: What should you do after sneezing into a tissue?
cards.back: Put the tissue in the bin and wash your hands.
cards.say: What should you do after sneezing into a tissue? Put the tissue in the bin and wash your hands.

cards.back: It makes the heart, muscles and bones stronger.
cards.say: Why is exercise important? It makes the heart, muscles and bones stronger.

cards.front: How much exercise do children need each day?
cards.back: About an hour of active play or sport.
cards.say: How much exercise do children need each day? About an hour of active play or sport.

cards.back: The body repairs itself and the brain rests.
cards.say: Why do we need sleep? The body repairs itself and the brain rests.

cards.front: Which keeps you healthy, sitting still all day or moving?
cards.back: Moving, because the body needs activity.
cards.say: Which keeps you healthy, sitting still all day or moving? Moving, because the body needs activity.

cards.back: Dirty water can carry germs that cause disease.
cards.say: Why is clean water important? Dirty water can carry germs that cause disease.

cards.front: Why do doctors give vaccines to children?
cards.back: To protect them from serious diseases.
cards.say: Why do doctors give vaccines to children? To protect them from serious diseases.

cards.front: True or false: Antibiotics work against viruses.
cards.back: False. Antibiotics only work on bacteria.
cards.say: True or false: Antibiotics work against viruses. False. Antibiotics only work on bacteria.

cards.front: True or false: All bacteria are harmful.
cards.back: False. Some bacteria help us, for example in digestion.
cards.say: True or false: All bacteria are harmful. False. Some bacteria help us, for example in digestion.
